newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso shuns rates fall to close firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso shuns rates fall to close firm.

text.p: The Mexican peso shunned the potentially adverse effects of falling primary rates to close firmer for the third day in a row on Wednesday, due to a continuing flow of foreign capital into Mexican financial markets, traders said.
"Apart from the fact that foreign capital has entered the market, local corporations are still long on dollars," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.1 and one centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8220/7.8270 and 7.8190/7.8240 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.9 centavos firmer at 7.8020/7.8120 per dollar.
"It's a one-way market even if most would still prefer the peso not to be so strong," the trader added.
Foreign capital inflow pushed Mexican stocks up 1.01 percent to a new intraday record high of 3,555.74 points shortly before the foreign exchange market closed.
Demand for secondary money market instruments meanwhile drove overnight Cetes rates down 125 basis points to 23.00 percent.

Dealers said foreign capital inflow was sufficiently heavy to offset the deleterious effect of greater-than-expected falls in primary rates, but noted that the bid-to-cover ratio was slightly down at the auction on Tuesday night.
The market was now focusing attention on December inflation figures, due to be released by Banco de Mexico on Thursday, traders said.
"It's difficult to say when the peso is likely to soften, as there are no sellers in the market," another trader said. ((--Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
